implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA: no trusted-time module exists (apps/mobile/src/data/trustedTime.ts absent), so lease expiry could only be judged by Date.now(). Defect in the r1 candidate (8e62e2c0, trustedTime.ts:260-313 trustedNow, 315-316 persist returns when !anchor, 415-427 checkpoint requires 'anchored'): in floor authority after relaunch the estimate was max(floor, wall-offset) with no monotonic pin and no re-persistence, so a wall clock wound back after a floor reading lowered the estimate undetected and a kill/reset/relaunch loop granted a fresh ~6-day lease each cycle. Round 2 (4 commits, tests before implementation each time): 1d6b7ad6 tests, fa271ddd implementation, b0e30394 foreground-checkpoint tests, 5d02b578 foreground-checkpoint implementation. Implementation: an in-process Mark {highWaterMs, monotonicAtMarkMs} is set on every trustedNow() so every later reading is >= mark + monotonic elapsed in every authority state (floor mode pinned to monotonic at first read); an adjusted wall clock more than 5 min below the estimate is rollbackDetected; persist() uses anchor ?? floor so floor-mode read()/checkpoint() re-persist the high-water mark (60s interval); evaluateLease() fails closed — rollback => reconcile_required/clock_rollback, floor-only authority can prove expiry but never an active lease (reconcile_required/floor_only), storage invalid/none => reconcile_required, issuedAt ahead of clock rejected, 7-day cap via OFFLINE_PRO_LEASE_MAX_SECONDS; server Date parsed only in strict IMF-fixdate form from authenticated responses, out-of-order responses cannot lower the clock (only an authenticated server can re-anchor lower). New in the last commit: createTrustedTime() takes an optional lifecycle (default React Native AppState, null disables); the first use subscribes once and every 'active' transition runs checkpoint(), so a wall clock seen ahead while the app was foregrounded is persisted and held against a later rollback even though performance.now() does not count device sleep. Wiring: api.ts feeds every authenticated response's Date header (preserved from r1). Adversary suite (attack-8e62e2c0) on the r2 module: ATTACK 1 (both P1 repro tests) now pass; remaining adversarial failures were two exact-value assertions that assume the floor never advances (incompatible with floor-mode checkpointing) and two static 'shipping consumer' checks (see residual_risks). non_blocking_issues: INFERRED (design, for W05-04 consumer): after a process relaunch the module only has `floor` authority and evaluateLease() returns reconcile_required/floor_only for any non-expired lease, so an offline Pro lease is never reported `active` again until an authenticated response re-anchors. This is the fail-closed choice the objective demands (performance.now() is process-relative, not device uptime; there is no cross-relaunch monotonic source in JS), but W05-04 must surface it honestly as 'reconnect to confirm remaining time' rather than 'lease expired'. A native system-uptime/boot-id bridge would be the way to restore offline availability across relaunch without weakening tamper resistance.

INFERRED: TrustedTimeLease uses epoch milliseconds while OfflineExecutionGrantClaims iat/exp (packages/shared-types offlineAuthorization.ts) are seconds; W05-04 must convert: a seconds-valued lease passed unconverted is a valid positive integer, so evaluateLease() would read it as a 1970 epoch-ms lease and report `expired` (fail-closed, but a false 'expired' for a live lease). The consumer needs a unit-conversion test.
